title: UMD Team Develops One of the Most Compact Heat Exchangers for Extreme Environments
summary: A University of Maryland CEEE team built a multi-pass microchannel heat exchanger for supercritical CO2 by selective laser melting, rated for above 800 °C and 80 bar. In tests it reached a power density of 45.4 MW/m³ with 11.75 W of pumping power and a surface area density of 989 m²/m³. The team says its literature survey makes this the most compact such exchanger reported. Design and test results were published in International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer in May and November 2025.
thermal: Compact sCO2 microchannel heat exchanger for high-temperature, high-pressure duty.
manufacturing: Selective laser melting of the whole multi-pass core, then hydraulic and thermal testing.

title: Developing a technology roadmap for STEP's sCO2 technology
summary: UK Industrial Fusion Solutions and UKAEA describe the power cycle chosen for the STEP fusion prototype (100 MWe net, operating in the 2040s): a transcritical CO2 cycle called SHOCC, with supercritical CO2 also planned for some in-vessel component cooling. The paper says compact printed circuit heat exchangers (PCHEs) are preferred for the primary-to-power-cycle exchanger and recuperators because of their maturity. It says no significant heat-exchanger scale-up programme is planned, since modules will stay near today's 50 MWth state of the art, but exchangers still need testing under rapid changes in operating conditions. A proof-of-concept rig is part of the roadmap.
thermal: Heat exchange from a tokamak to an sCO2 power cycle, and sCO2 cooling of in-vessel parts.
manufacturing: PCHEs (diffusion-bonded etched plates) are the preferred construction; no printing discussed.

title: Thermohydraulic performance of a supercritical CO2 PCHE for heat pipe microreactors
summary: University of Wisconsin-Madison and UNICAMP designed, built and tested a sub-sized printed circuit heat exchanger to couple a 5 MWth heat-pipe microreactor to a recompression sCO2 Brayton cycle. The diffusion-bonded stainless-steel test piece was heated by cartridge heaters and mapped with fibre-optic temperature sensors in the WisCO2 facility, at up to 325 °C, 10 MPa and 0.16 kg/s. The authors report efficient heat transfer and predictable pressure drop and offer the data as a benchmark for CFD.
thermal: Heat-pipe-to-sCO2 primary heat exchanger for a microreactor.
manufacturing: Etched and diffusion-bonded stainless plates; fibre-optic solid temperature mapping in test.

title: Adjoint-based Topology Optimization - Maximizing Heat Transfer of a Brake Cooling Duct
summary: A Siemens Digital Industries Software presentation shows level-set adjoint topology optimisation in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ of a brake cooling duct, maximising heat transfer on the front rotor under volume and pressure-drop limits. The optimised duct is put back into the car model to check the real gain, and a further adjoint shape step can improve it. It says additive manufacturing makes the shape producible. No numbers or tests are given.
thermal: Brake rotor cooling by duct airflow.
manufacturing: Topology optimisation for printing; no build.

title: Flow boiling heat transfer and pressure drop in gyroid and diamond TPMS channels
summary: Seoul National University of Science and Technology measured flow boiling of R-1234yf in printed monolithic aluminium gyroid and diamond TPMS channels (seven cells each; 20-80 kg/m²s, 5-30 kW/m², vapour quality 0.08-0.91). In boiling, the gyroid gave up to 165% higher heat transfer coefficient for up to 17.4% more pressure drop than the diamond, while the diamond was better in single-phase flow. The authors conclude the gyroid is the better choice for evaporators.
